Featured research

Browse audits

Maritime crisis management

When does a maritime crisis end?

A withdrawal can end a confrontation and leave the underlying dispute unresolved. Theme 44 compares Scarborough Shoal with other maritime disputes to show what the public record can establish about how a crisis ended.

Read the thematic memo View evidence

Naval strategy

How did far seas protection become part of China’s naval strategy?

Jennifer Rice and Erik Robb trace the idea through earlier policy and peacetime missions. The 2015 and 2019 defense white papers use different terms in English, giving readers a way to follow the strategy’s public formulation.

Read the paper analysis View evidence

Chinese intelligence history

How did the Chinese Communist Party build its intelligence institutions?

Peter Mattis and Matthew Brazil trace the institutional changes that followed the transition from revolutionary movement to governing party. The audit follows the formation of the Central Investigation Department and its place in that history.

Read the chapter analysis View evidence

Reading paths

What drives decisions in a maritime crisis?

  1. Paper Chinese Nationalism and the “Gray Zone” Andrew Chubb asks when public opinion influenced maritime policy.
  2. Memo Decision-Making Under Uncertainty During Crises Trace what the public record can tell us about what leaders knew at the time.
  3. Profile Andrew Chubb and fellow Red Book authors See how Chubb and other contributors use different evidence to study maritime disputes.

From far seas protection to naval diplomacy

  1. Paper Naval Diplomacy with Chinese Characteristics Timothy R. Heath examines how China uses naval diplomacy to build international relationships.
  2. Memo How China Builds a Far-Seas Presence Read the diplomacy report alongside studies of the Gulf of Aden escorts and overseas ports.
  3. Profile The institutions behind China’s defense white papers See how the State Council Information Office and Ministry of National Defense publish policy and explain events.

Researching China’s intelligence institutions

  1. Paper Chinese Communist Intelligence Organizations Start with the development of the Party’s intelligence institutions before and after 1949.
  2. Memo What the publication series let us verify The chapter extracts omit the book’s endnotes. See what that means for checking the citations.
  3. Profile Peter Mattis and Matthew Brazil Explore the authors’ research backgrounds and the chapters covered by the dashboard.

Batch history · Batch 8 spotlight
DOCS #71–#80 · NAVAL INSTITUTE PRESS

CCP Espionage & Surveillance (1927–2019), Rear Adm. McDevitt's 21st-Century Naval Power & Barton Whaley's Deception Methodology

Ten foundational Naval Institute Press chapters (118 PDF pages, 577 endnotes, 40 audited rows [38 ok, 2 fix], 8 shared source clusters, 6 synthesis memos).

Browse Batch 8 reports
Cluster A · Docs #71–#73 (CCE) 2019 · 36 pp. · 253 notes

Mattis & Brazil: CCP Intelligence Orgs, Espionage Cases & Domestic Surveillance

Audits 3 chapters (CCE-C1, CCE-C6, CCE-C7): evolution from 1927 Teke, PPB, SAD, and CID to 2PLA/JSD/SSF and the 18-bureau MSS; cyber-HUMINT fusion (OPM/Taiwan database hacks + JSSD/Xu Yanjun aviation ring); 34 U.S./Taiwan/European espionage case entries; and PRC 'baseline surveillance' (shenfen zheng, hukou, dang'an, Alibaba Zhima Credit, and 6 intensive MPS/MSS methods).

Audit Catch (CCEC6-R02 · fix): Caught p. 5 calling James Fondren Col. James Fondren, USA (Ret.) while p. 7 calls him a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel (plus MMS typo for MSS in CCE-C7).
Cluster B · Docs #74–#79 (CN21) 2020 · 77 pp. · 320 notes

Rear Adm. McDevitt: China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power (6 Chapters)

Audits 6 chapters (CN21-C1 to C5, C8): Hu/Xi maritime great-power timelines & 'SLOC anxiety'; 1985–2008 voyages (Tables 1–2) & 12 years of Gulf of Aden escorts (33 rotations, 27,000 sailors, Djibouti base); 131 blue-water ships built since 2004 & Table 3 global comparison; sequenced Taiwan campaign (Tables 4–6, RAND airbase TBM math, 56-sub wolf-pack shortfall, July 2019 6-missile DF-21D test); Xi's 'Five Cannots'; and the 2035 425-ship PLAN forecast.

Audit Catch (CN21C1-R01 · fix): Caught p. 9 misdating Xi's Oct 2017 19th Party Congress report to October 2018 (contradicting pp. 1 & 5). Verified 100% of Tables 1–6.
Cluster C · Doc #80 (PTD-P1) 2016 · 5 pp. · Chs. 1–3

Barton Whaley: Practise to Deceive Part One (Intent, Scope & Sources)

Completes our 5-part audit of Whaley's magnum opus (PTD-P1 joining PTD-00, PTD-C6, PTD-C7, PTD-P3): documents the July 6, 1987 RAND proposal to Feer & Whelan (57 cases for Fort Irwin OPFOR exercises, expanded to 88 cases), the 3 computerized databases (DECEPTR 230 cases & NTC 140 cases), the CIA Library Whaley Collection, and debunking myths about Eisenhower, Mark Clark & Montgomery.

Audit Verification (4/4 ok): Verified the 57+31=88 case math, DECEPTR/NTC database structure, and Col. Meinertzhagen fabricated-memoir critique.
